new_statements.relation_note: Defines Trochaic Zapotec (which includes Totomachapan as a first-order branch) by the stress shift *CVˈCV > *ˈCVCV; gives Totomachapan forms with initial stress marks; states there is no tonal data for Totomachapan ('requires research'); notes Western Relic Area languages do not develarize *kw in the final (post-tonic) syllable.
new_statements.rule_in_words: By subgrouping: Totomachapan is a Trochaic Zapotec language, i.e. it shares the innovation *CVˈCV > *ˈCVCV (stress retracted to the root-initial/penultimate syllable of disyllabic roots); the author's own phonetic transcriptions of Totomachapan survey forms mark stress on the root-initial syllable ([ˈn-aʃu] 'CONT-lie.down', [ˈn-duku] 'CONT-sit', [ˈaʂi], [ˈuʂi]) where Proto-Zapotecan/Chatino have final stress (*n-tuˈkwa, /n-tuˈkwa/). Tone: explicitly no data ('Totomachapan requires research').
new_statements.exceptions: none for Totomachapan; prefixes are outside the stress domain ('syllabic prefixes are unstressed when added to consonant-stems', p.13, said of Zapotecan languages that retain unstressed vowels)

new_statements.quote: All modern Zapotec languages descend from Proto Trochaic Zapotec (PTZ). Proto-Zapotec and PTZ differ due to a stress shift that is reflected in all modern languages but which philological evidence indicates did not occur in Soltec. [...] We have no tonal data for Soltec, and very little information about Soltec verbal morphology. [...] Since PTZ times, the root-initial syllable has been the most prominent in the phonological word. This syllable is stressed by Hyman's (2006: 231) definition. I will refer to stressed syllables as "tonic syllables" and to the unstressed syllables that precede and follow as "pre-tonic" and "post-tonic." (p.5) [...] Trochaic Zapotec languages all reflect a shift in which any disyllabic roots with stress on the ultima shifted it to the penult (Beam de Azcona In Preparation). (p.44)

new_statements.relation_note: Root-initial stress ('tonic syllable') characterises all Trochaic Zapotec languages, among which Totomachapan is explicitly classified; Totomachapan verb forms carry tone diacritics in the author's transcription (data only); early Zapotecan tone reconstructed as /H, L, Ø/ per mora without Totomachapan evidence.
new_statements.rule_in_words: All modern Zapotec languages, Totomachapan included (Figure 1 places it inside Trochaic Zapotec), have the root-initial syllable as the stressed/tonic syllable (disyllabic roots: penult); Totomachapan forms are cited with tone diacritics (e.g. rising on [j-y̌nːa]) but no tonal analysis of Totomachapan is offered, and the reconstruction of tone explicitly cannot use Soltec/Totomachapan data.
new_statements.exceptions: none specific to Totomachapan; pre-tonic (prefix) and post-tonic syllables unstressed by definition
